source_records.source: GTEx Portal API v2 (gtex_v8, GENCODE v26, GRCh38/hg38) median gene expression for CD28 (ENSG00000178562.17)
Bgee REST API v15 (macaca_mulatta, NCBITaxon:9544, genome Mmul_10) expression calls for CD28 (ENSMMUG00000057214)

limitations: Incompatible quantitative scales (no cross-species fold changes): human GTEx (gtex_v8) reports bulk RNA-Seq median Transcripts Per Million (TPM), whereas Bgee reports a non-parametric rank-normalised expressionScore (0-100) and FDR-controlled present calls integrated across RNA-Seq, Affymetrix microarrays, in situ hybridization, and ESTs. Ratios or fold changes between GTEx TPM and Bgee expressionScore are mathematically invalid and are never computed.

Missing animal tissue annotations do not establish biological absence: Bgee returned 7 tissue-level UBERON expression calls for CD28 in macaca_mulatta (2 exact UBERON matches with GTEx). Human tissues lacking a corresponding Bgee call represent unsampled or unannotated anatomical entities in Bgee for that species, not absence of expression.

Anatomical ontology granularity differences: GTEx frequently annotates surgical biopsy sub-structures (e.g. right lobe of liver UBERON:0001114, lower lobe of left lung UBERON:0008952, venous blood UBERON:0013756, sigmoid/transverse colon UBERON:0001159/UBERON:0001157), whereas Bgee often aggregates calls at the parent organ level (liver UBERON:0002107, lung UBERON:0002048, blood UBERON:0000178, colon UBERON:0001155); sub-structure and whole-organ terms are reported separately.

Bulk tissue homogenate confounding and mRNA-versus-protein gap: whole-tissue RNA measurements average across parenchymal, stromal, endothelial, and infiltrating immune cells (e.g. T-cell transcripts in bulk spleen, blood, lung, or gut) and do not measure translated protein abundance, cell-surface receptor density, or isoform-specific subcellular targeting (such as ENT1/SLC29A1 mitochondrial localisation).
